summary: Iwao Nakajima studied at Hitotsubashi University under Nichiki Kimura. He held a post at the NHK Broadcasting Culture Research Institute until 1975 and served as head at Sandhaan (attested 1999).
Iwao Shima was a scholar of Indology and philosophy who studied at Nagoya University. He served at Kanazawa University, where he is attested in 1992 and as professor in 2003.

Izumi Hoshi is a Tibetologist and linguist who completed undergraduate and graduate studies at the University of Tokyo between circa 1987 and 1997. She served as assistant professor (1997) and director (2019–2023) at Tokyo University of Foreign Studies.
Izumi Matsuda-Kiami works in linguistics and Japanology. Educated at the University of Wisconsin-Madison, she is an attested teaching professor at the University of Washington (2026).

J. A. B. van Buitenen was an Indology and philosophy scholar who earned his doctorate at Utrecht University under Jan Gonda (1946–1953). He held posts at Deccan College, Utrecht University (1959–1961), and the University of Chicago (1957–1964).
J. B. Disanayaka is a scholar in linguistics and Indology. In 1996, he held an attested professorship at the University of Colombo and a post at SOAS University of London.

J. Gordon Melton, a religious studies scholar, studied at Birmingham-Southern College, Garrett-Evangelical Theological Seminary, and Northwestern University. He founded the Institute for the Study of American Religion and held posts at UC Santa Barbara (circa 1985–2011) and Baylor University (circa 2011).

J. J. C. Smart was a philosopher who studied at the University of Glasgow and The Queen's College, Oxford. He held academic posts at the University of Adelaide (~1950–1972), La Trobe University (~1972–1976), and the Australian National University (~1976–1985).

Sinologist J. J. L. Duyvendak studied at Leiden, the Sorbonne, and Berlin, learning under Édouard Chavannes and Henri Cordier. After serving at the Dutch Legation in Peking (1912–1918), he taught at Leiden University from 1919 and was professor from 1930 to 1954.
J. M. E. McTaggart was a philosopher who was educated at Clifton College (~1882–1885). He held a post at the University of Cambridge from circa 1897 to 1923.
J. Mark G. Williams is a scholar in Buddhist studies who studied at the Massachusetts Institute of Technology. He served as director at the University of Oxford from circa 2003 to 2016.

J. P. Mallory is a scholar of archaeology, linguistics, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. Educated at Occidental College and UCLA, he held long-term posts at Queen's University Belfast (~1977–2011) and Queen's University at Kingston (attested 2014).

J. Thomas Rimer is a Japanology scholar educated at Princeton and Columbia University. He held positions at Washington University in St. Louis (~1971–1983), the University of Maryland, College Park (~1988–1997), and the University of Pittsburgh (~1997–2008), among others.
Jaan Puhvel studied under Stig Wikander (~1952–1953) and Georges Dumézil (~1954–1955), and later taught C. Scott Littleton.

Jack Copeland is a philosopher who studied at Corpus Christi College, Oxford, completing his doctorate under Dana Scott (~1975–1979). He has held academic posts at the University of Portsmouth and the University of Canterbury (1985).

Jack Goody was a scholar of history and archaeology. He was educated at St Albans School and St John's College, Cambridge (~1938–1954), and held a post at the University of Cambridge from circa 1984 to 2015.

Jack Kornfield works in Buddhist and religious studies. Educated at Dartmouth and Saybrook University, he studied under Ajahn Chah, Wing-tsit Chan, Mahasi Sayadaw, and Dipa Ma. He co-founded the Insight Meditation Society and Spirit Rock Meditation Center.
Jack Laughlin is a scholar of Indology and religious studies who completed his PhD at McMaster University in 1999. He held a post at the University of Sudbury.

Jacob Dalton specializes in Tibetology and Buddhist studies, earning his PhD at the University of Michigan under Donald S. Lopez Jr. (2002). He held posts at SOAS, Yale University (2005), and the University of California, Berkeley (attested 2011–2026).

Jacob Ensink was an Indologist who completed his doctorate at Utrecht University under Jan Gonda (~1946–1952). In 1954, he joined the University of Groningen, where he served as lecturer and later professor.
